This miscellaneous second appeal, under section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "FSSA") has been filed against the judgment dated 8/5/2024 passed by appellate Authority/
IX District Judge, Gwalior in RCA No.23 of 2024, as well as, order dated 21/11/2023 passed by Adjudicating Officer/ Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/147/2021.
2.

sentences.text: Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 22/3/2021, Food Safety Officer collected samples of Namkeen which was being manufactured by the appellant.
In the complaint, it is mentioned that the manufacturing was being done in a most unhygienic manner and on a dirty floor.
It was informed by the appellant that the Namkeen is meant for sale.

Accordingly,
four packets of the special Namkeen of 1 kg each, 2 kgs of loose Besan, two litres of refined palmolein oil (loose), 2 kg Deepak brand wheat floor were collected by way of samples from the shop o f t h e a p p e l l a n t . A l l t h e f o u r s a m p l e s w e r e s e a l e d N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

as per law and, accordingly, they were sent to the Laboratory.

The Food Analyst, as per his report (Ex.P/25), found that Namkeen Jain Special Namkeen (Pack) was misbranded, Palmolein Oil Ref. palmolein oil (loose) was found to be substandard vide report (Ex.P/26) and Wheat flour wheat flour was also found to be misbranded as per report (Ex.P/30), whereas Besan was found within norms.

3. The Adjudicating Officer by the impugned order held that the appellant is guilty of committing offence under section 51, 52, 56 and 58 of FSSA and accordingly imposed a penalty of Rs. 50,000/-
for violation of section 51, Rs.
20,000/- for violation of section 52, Rs. 10,000/- for violation of section 56 and Rs. 20,000/- for violation of section 58.
Being aggrieved by the said order, appellant preferred an appeal which too has been dismissed by the impugned order passed by the IX District Judge Gwalior/ appellate Authority.

entities.text: IX District Judge Gwalior/ appellate Authority
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Challenging the orders passed by the Court below/Adjudicating Officer, a solitary ground was raised by counsel for appellant that the penalty imposed by the Authorities is on a higher side and,
therefore, it may be reduced.

5. Heard learned counsel for the appellant.
6.
From the complaint, it is clear that at the time of inspection it was found that the Namkeen was being prepared in a most unhygienic manner and the raw material was lying on the dirty floor.

The inspection note (Ex.P/14) was prepared and it has been mentioned as under:-
".....                   
       (unhygienic and unhealthy)        
                 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31096 3 MSA-6-2024    , , ,
,                  ....."
7.
Thus it is clear that not only the palmolein oil was found to be substandard but even Jain special Namkeen and wheat flour were found to be misbranded.

Under these circumstances, penalty of Rs.
50,000/- for violation of section 51, Rs. 20,000/- for violation of section 52, Rs. 10,000/- for violation of section 56 and Rs. 20,000/- for violation of section 58 cannot be said to be on higher side.
8. No other argument is advanced by counsel for appellant.
9. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out for warranting interference.

10. Accordingly the judgment dated 8/5/2024 passed by appellate Authority/ IX District Judge,
Gwalior in RCA No.23 of 2024, as well as, order dated 21/11/2023 passed by Adjudicating Officer/
Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/147/2021 are hereby affirmed.
